review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked the candidates I thought most likely to duplicate existing concepts. I found no avoidable competing concept.

- **`Bundle.zeroSection`:** it is the only zero-section definition in Mathlib, so it has no competitor.
- **`VectorBundleCore` and `VectorBundleCore.toFiberBundleCore`:** these are a deliberate linear specialisation of `FiberBundleCore`. The core is connected to the general one through `toFiberBundleCore`, so the two are integrated rather than competing.
- **`Index`, `Base`, `Fiber`:** these mirror the `FiberBundleCore` convenience definitions on purpose, for dot notation and typeclass inference.
- **`Pretrivialization.IsLinear`/`linearMapAt`/`symmₗ` and the `Trivialization` versions:** the `Trivialization` declarations are defined by delegation to the `Pretrivialization` ones. Each pair is a named API at its own level, not an independent redundant definition.
- **`coordChangeL`:** it is the continuous-linear-equiv version of the fiber-bundle coordinate change, and the file gives lemmas relating the two.
- **`VectorPrebundle`:** it is built on `FiberPrebundle` through `toFiberPrebundle`.
- **`ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates`:** I found no existing Mathlib counterpart, and its docstring explains why it is defined everywhere.

I could not rule out an equivalent concept elsewhere in Mathlib, but my searches (mainly for `zeroSection` and `Core` definitions) turned up nothing.
